Oct 21, 2027 - Koranvistani Annexation of the Massanikoan Islands

The Government of Massanikos Collapsed on the 14th of June, earlier in the year. Though the islanders had been getting along well enough with their remaining government infrastructure, international support had fallen by the wayside. Early in October, the provisional body sent a letter to Koranvistan, due to the large numbers of Hellenic Grigoriyans within the Kingdom. Acknowledging their shared cultural histories, proximity, and EDU membership, the provisional body offered annexation of the Massanikoan Islands in exchange for, essentially, the status quo.
Over the course of a few weeks, negotiations took place on the main island, and a document was signed. Set to go into effect on the 21st, the provisional government held a vote among the islanders on the annexation, and the move was popular. When the day came, the Koranvistan Travel Agency unveiled their new Island Ferry Service, connecting the new additions to the mainland. A small dispatch, led by Minister Malenkova and Minister Sasanov, took the ferry to the islands to welcome the new District Government into the Kingdom.
The first order of business was conducting research on the Island Districts education, employment opportunities, infrastructure, and quality of life. The new Kingdom Integration Board, a subsection of the new Royal Affairs Ministry, would be conducting the study with the help of Velnaz University students and reporting their findings to the Internal Affairs Ministry. Any shortfalls from the lapse in power structure would be fixed and brought up to both Massanikoan and Kingdom standards.

[b]October 22-28, 2027: The Purge[/b]

The SCSID, moving to ensure the continuance of the D-29 doctrines focus on military efficiency, would order a silent purge of the top generals of the armed forces, quietly moving into their place top SCSID leadership who had experience within those particular branches. 

To ensure a public message was sent to the national and international communities, the SCSID would quietly push the assembly to hold a public disavowal of allegiance of a few crucial selected generals. 

Thus, on October 23, the grand assembly in a televised session would bring forward twelve generals from the army, accusing them of treason and other trumped-up charges; they would be formally stripped of their pay and rank, before being led out of the assembly hall by SCSID officers.

Following the 23rd,  the process would be repeated on live television until the 28th of October, with Strømm making an appearance at the final trial to make a statement, The unity of the armed forces is paramount to the stability of the nation, the safety of the citizens was at stake, with these corrupt generals, but now, we have ensured that the radical and dangerous elements of the armed forces have been removed, and the leadership cleaned up for maximum efficiency,
